facts.raw_span: A 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
receiving maintenance therapy (daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone)
3 months of hematochezia
two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood
polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
abdomen was soft and nontender
a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted
Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains

concepts.why: The presence of multiple semisessile polyps with surrounding erythematous mucosa and histiocytes containing basophilic inclusions is unusual and points to gastrointestinal histiocytosis.

support_spans: two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood
contradict_spans: polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding
concepts.why: The presence of chronic hematochezia and loose bowel movements with mixed blood is consistent with inflammatory bowel disease, but the lack of response to polyethylene glycol and the presence of specific histological findings argue against it.

The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes that are positive on von Kossa and periodic acid-Schiff stains, in a patient with a history of immunosuppression due to T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia and negative stool studies for common pathogens, suggests Whipple disease.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains is a decisive finding for Gastrointestinal histiocytosis.
